samples.summary: copyThread detaches a thread anchor with detachYorkieValue, which mangles the docs-range `posRange` array (and may recurse into CRDT internals)
samples.evidence: `copyThread` does `anchor: (detachYorkieValue(t.anchor) ?? {})`. The docblock this same PR added to `yorkie-json.ts` (lines 13-20) states that `detachYorkieValue` "branches on `Array.isArray`, which is false for a Yorkie array proxy, so a chart's `seriesColumns` or a slide's `elements` would come back as `{createdAt, movedAt}` CRDT metadata". A `docs-range` anchor's `posRange` is exactly such a nested array (`TreePosStructRange = [TreePosStruct, TreePosStruct]`, see packages/frontend/src/types/comments.ts:31), so every `doc`-document thread returned by `GET /comments`, `POST /:threadId/replies` (via mutateThread→copyThread) and `PATCH /:threadId` carries a garbage anchor instead of the tree positions. The frontend's `copyDocsThread` (yorkie-comment-store.ts:81-88) deliberately does NOT copy `posRange` for precisely this reason. Worse case: if `Object.entries` on the CRDTArray target exposes its `elements` (RGATreeList, doubly-linked), the recursive walk hits a cycle and throws a RangeError → 500 on every doc-thread read/edit. Also on the authorization path, since `findComment`/`rootCommentId` both call `copyThread`.

samples.summary: duplicateTab copies a worksheet verbatim, so charts/pivots on the copy still source the ORIGINAL tab id
samples.evidence: `const copy: Worksheet = { ...worksheet, comments: {} }; root.sheets[newTabId] = copy;` — only `comments` is cleared. A `SheetChart` carries `sourceTabId` (packages/sheets/src/model/workbook/worksheet-document.ts:20) and the editor creates self-sourced charts with `sourceTabId: tabId` (frontend sheet-view.tsx:421). After `POST /tabs/:tabId/duplicate`, every chart (and any `pivotTable`) on the copy still points at the source tab, so the duplicated tab renders the original tab's data and stops tracking edits made to the copy. The copy is therefore not an independent duplicate, which is what the endpoint advertises ("Copy a tab and its grid next to it").

samples.summary: An unknown layoutId is silently accepted and produces a slide built from a different layout
samples.evidence: `addSlide` passes `layoutId` straight to `MemSlidesStore.addSlide`, whose `resolveLayout` is `this.doc.layouts.find(...) ?? getLayout(layoutId)` (packages/slides/src/store/memory.ts:173) and `getLayout` returns `BUILT_IN_LAYOUTS.find(...) ?? BUILT_IN_LAYOUTS[0]` (packages/slides/src/model/layout.ts:197). So `POST .../slides {"layoutId":"typo"}` answers 200 with a slide built from the first built-in layout instead of rejecting — the very failure the new `GET /layouts` catalog exists to prevent. No 400 path exists for a bad layout id.

samples.summary: parsePdfAnchor accepts degenerate and off-page rectangles
samples.evidence: The per-key check is only `value < 0 || value > 1`, so `w: 0` / `h: 0` (a zero-area, unclickable anchor) is accepted, and `{x: 0.9, w: 0.9}` produces a rectangle extending past the right edge of the page. Nothing later re-validates the rect, and the thread is written into the CRDT, so the viewer gets an anchor it cannot render meaningfully.

samples.summary: "last slide" / "last tab" / pivot-dependent refusals are evaluated on the pre-update read, outside doc.update
samples.evidence: `deleteSlide` decides `doc.slides.length <= 1` on the detached read and `applySlideChange`'s `remove` branch re-checks nothing (`if (at >= 0) slides.splice(at, 1)`). The same shape exists in `tabs.controller.ts#remove`, where `resolveDelete` (last_tab / pivot_dependents) runs on `doc.getRoot()` before `doc.update`. A concurrent delete landing between the read and the update leaves a deck with zero slides / a workbook with zero tabs, i.e. exactly the invariant these refusals exist to protect.

samples.summary: 'insert' change resolves its landing position by index while 'insert-after'/'remove'/'move' resolve by id
samples.evidence: `applySlideChange`'s `insert` branch clamps `change.index` computed against the *read* snapshot, so a concurrent insert earlier in the deck shifts the new slide onto a different position than requested — the exact hazard the `insert-after`/`afterId` design comment (lines 60-66) says these changes carry ids to avoid.

samples.summary: Slides read through readSlidesRoot loses meta.slideHeight, so an added slide on a non-16:9 deck can be laid out against the 1080 canvas
samples.evidence: `readSlidesRoot` (slides-tree.ts:69-80) rebuilds `meta` as only `{title, themeId, masterId}`. slide-ops's own docblock acknowledges the drop for the write path, but the dropped `slideHeight` is also an *input* to layout resolution/rescaling (`packages/slides/src/model/layout.ts:200-208`, memory.ts:482 comment). For a deck that has no `layouts[]` of its own (falls back to `BUILT_IN_LAYOUTS` authored against height 1080), `POST .../slides` on an imported 4:3 deck seeds placeholder frames in the wrong vertical space.

`edited` is only assigned when `applyEditComment` finds the comment; on `undefined` the handler still returns `{ threadId, comment: undefined }` with a 200 rather than a 404. It is currently shielded by `assertCommentAuthor`, but the two lookups are independent (authorize reads a detached copy before `doc.update`, the mutate reads the live map inside it), so a concurrent delete of that comment yields a success response for a write that did not happen.

samples.summary: parseRef accepts lowercase A1 refs, so 'b2' validates as column 33 rather than 2
samples.evidence: `parseRef` (packages/sheets/src/model/core/coordinates.ts:341-347) computes the column from `charCodeAt(0) - 65` with no case handling and no upper bound, so `'b2'` yields `{r:2,c:33}` instead of throwing. `parseImages` therefore stores `anchor: 'b2'` as a "valid A1 reference", and `sheetCellAnchor` in comments.controller.ts:653 reports the misleading "has no stable row/column id yet" 400 instead of "invalid reference".

verdict.reason: The finding checks out at every step. comment-ops.ts:99 does pass the thread anchor through detachYorkieValue, and detachYorkieValue (yorkie-json.ts:153-186) dispatches on Array.isArray, which the repo itself twice documents as false for a Yorkie array proxy (yorkie-json.ts:14-20 and worksheet-charts.controller.ts:58-66, "the array comes back as {createdAt, movedAt} CRDT metadata"), so nested arrays fall into the Object.entries branch and are walked as CRDT internals. A docs-range anchor holds exactly such a nested array: posRange: TreePosStructRange (frontend/src/types/comments.ts:28-33), written as a Yorkie array at yorkie-comment-store.ts:180-198, whose own copyDocsThread docblock (lines 77-108) deliberately keeps it as a live proxy because it does not round-trip. The backend reads a live root proxy, not a plain snapshot: comments.controller.ts:250-257 calls listThreads(doc.getRoot().comments) for doc/pdf types, and listThreads -> copyThread (comment-ops.ts:133-141); mutateThread (comments.controller.ts:588-604) and the auth helpers findComment (comment-ops.ts:217) / rootCommentId (comments.controller.ts:614) hit the same copyThread. No guard anywhere strips or special-cases posRange (grep for posRange across packages/backend finds only comments and plain-object fixtures), and the only anchor-detachment test (comment-ops.spec.ts:263-283) uses a plain object, so the proxy case is unexercised. Whether the walk returns CRDT metadata or recurses into RGATreeList's cyclic links, doc-document threads come back with a wrong or exploding anchor on a normally reachable route. No refutation ground applies.

verdict.reason: The finding is accurate on every checked point. tab-ops.ts:167 copies the worksheet with only `comments` cleared (`const copy: Worksheet = { ...worksheet, comments: {} }`), so `charts` and `pivotTable` are carried verbatim into the new tab at line 168. SheetChart holds a `sourceTabId` (worksheet-document.ts:20) and the editor creates self-sourced charts with `sourceTabId: tabId` (sheet-view.tsx:421). Chart data resolution reads `root.sheets[chart.sourceTabId]` (chart-utils.ts:116, 188, 281), and pivots likewise (use-pivot-table.ts:135), so after POST /tabs/:tabId/duplicate (tabs.controller.ts:238-271) every self-sourced chart on the copy renders the ORIGINAL tab's grid and ignores edits made to the copy. The endpoint/CLI advertise a full grid copy with comments as the only stated exclusion (cli/src/commands/tabs.ts:174-177), so this breaks the advertised contract. No guard or remapping exists anywhere: tab-ops.spec.ts:178-213 covers only placement, naming and comment-clearing, and the only duplicate-time id remapping precedent in the repo is for slides (yorkie-slides-store.ts:739-749), not tabs. Cross-tab charts should legitimately retain their sourceTabId, so the fix must be selective, but that does not make the current self-sourced behavior correct. Reachable on a normal path, leaves the duplicate in an inconsistent state -> major; no refutation ground applies.

finding.summary: `withSref` hands a live Yorkie array proxy to `cellAnchorToSref`, unlike every existing caller which detaches with `Array.from` first
finding.evidence: `withSref` passes `worksheet.rowOrder ?? []` and `worksheet.colOrder ?? []` straight into `cellAnchorToSref`, which calls `order.rowOrder.indexOf(anchor.rowId)` (packages/sheets/src/comment/anchor.ts:26-27). Both existing call sites detach first — `rowOrder: Array.from(ws.rowOrder ?? []) as string[]` at packages/frontend/src/app/documents/document-detail.tsx:276 and :763. If the array proxy does not expose `indexOf`, every `GET .../comments` and every sheet thread creation 500s. Counter-evidence I found: `root.tabOrder.indexOf(tabId)` is used on a live root proxy at document-detail.tsx:474, which suggests `indexOf` does exist and this is only a divergence from the established detach-first convention (plus an O(N) CRDT walk per thread on a dense axis). Flagging at low confidence for the verifier to settle.

verdict.reason: The code is as described — withSref (comments.controller.ts:703-714) hands live Yorkie array proxies to cellAnchorToSref, which calls .indexOf (sheets/src/comment/anchor.ts:26-27), while the frontend detaches with Array.from (document-detail.tsx:276-277, :763-764). But the asserted failure (every GET/POST 500s because the proxy lacks indexOf) is refuted by counterexample: this repo already calls .indexOf on live Yorkie array proxies in core, shipped paths — backend tab-ops.ts:124 on the read-side root from tabs.controller.ts:226 (real SDK Document per yorkie.service.ts:42-46), tab-ops.ts:105/:170 inside doc.update (tabs.controller.ts:186-188, :264-266), and frontend document-detail.tsx:474/:481 for tab deletion. If indexOf threw or failed to match string ids, tab move/delete would already be broken. What is left is a convention divergence plus an O(N) axis walk (Array.from is equally O(N)) — no wrong condition, missing guard, crash, data loss, or async fault, so nothing blocking under the Correctness rubric.
